cohort: Low-risk parous women with nonanomalous singletons who had at least one prior vaginal delivery after 20 weeks and delivered at or after 39 weeks.
finding: Elective induction of labor at 39 weeks in low-risk parous women was associated with decreased odds of cesarean delivery and maternal adverse outcomes, with no significant difference in neonatal adverse outcomes compared to expectant management.
mod_finding: Elective induction at 39 weeks was associated with a lower rate of cesarean delivery compared to expectant management.
